slides.say: Dana bought a dress at a discount of forty shekels. The price of the dress after the discount was x shekels. What was the discount on the dress, in percent?
There's an x in the choices, so we can plug in numbers. [short pause] We'll solve it by plugging in, and then with a line of algebra.
at: There's an x in the choices

slides.say: First, what is a percent? Percent means out of a hundred. A discount of forty shekels on a price of a hundred shekels is a discount of forty percent. The percent always compares to the whole price, the price before the discount.
at: Percent means out of a hundred

slides.say: So where do we put a number? In percent questions we put a hundred, and we put it at the whole. Why? Some students put the hundred at x, the price after the discount. Then the price before is a hundred forty, and we'd need forty out of a hundred forty. That's not a nice calculation.
at: Some students put the hundred at x

slides.say: So we put the hundred at the price before. The discount is forty, so the price after is a hundred minus forty, sixty. So x is sixty.
And the discount is forty out of a hundred, forty percent. So the right choice must give forty when x is sixty.
Now we rule out whatever isn't forty. Choice number one, forty times a hundred, over sixty plus forty. Sixty plus forty is a hundred, and the hundreds cancel. That leaves forty, so it stays.
Choice number two, forty times sixty, over a hundred. Forty times sixty is two thousand four hundred, and over a hundred is twenty-four. Out.
Choice number three, sixty plus forty, over a hundred. A hundred over a hundred is one. Out.
Choice number four, a hundred times a hundred, over forty. A hundred over forty is two and a half, and times a hundred it's two hundred fifty. Out. So choice number one is our answer.
at: So choice number one is our answer

slides.say: [pause] With algebra, the price before is x plus forty. The discount in percent is forty out of x plus forty, times a hundred. That's choice number one. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: the price before is x plus forty
